lockedConditions: 100 people, initially known OFF persistent one-bit light state, one entrant at a time.
A strategy may be agreed beforehand; after isolation only the switch communicates and each person retains private memory.
The entrant order is arbitrary and every person is selected infinitely often if the process continues forever.
One correct announcement that everyone has visited at least once; no fixed deadline and no promise of uniform random selection.

R2.announcementTimingDifference: The source announces at its last ON observation after n−2 prior turn-OFF actions. This episode instead performs the last OFF/increment before announcing. The variant is an explicit design choice, to be verified in the episode model.

episodeIndependentReasoning.status: Protocol and proof requirements established; executable-model results are owned by the separate model agent and not claimed by this research.
episodeIndependentReasoning.safety: Each non-counter sends at most once; every counted ON has a distinct unsent-origin signal because initial light is OFF and only the counter clears it. Count n−1 implies every non-counter has visited; the counter is visiting at announcement.
episodeIndependentReasoning.progress: Under every-person-infinitely-often scheduling, an ON signal is eventually consumed by the counter; if OFF and someone unsent remains, such a person eventually visits and sends. Repeating finitely many stages gives eventual termination. This reasoning is independent of a uniform distribution.
episodeIndependentReasoning.deadline: For any finite proposed visit bound, a fair schedule may delay one still-unsent person beyond that finite prefix and remain fair thereafter. No fixed worst-case bound follows from fairness.
episodeIndependentReasoning.visualKnowledgeBoundary: An instructional full roster, true pending sender or visited/sent sets may be shown only as an explicitly global teaching view. Each prisoner acts only from role, current bit and private memory.
